B.4.1 CAPEX Captial Expenditures associated with standing up a high power test stand are significant. A single C-Band RF power klystron capable of 50MW peak powers and the associated modulator will cost approximately $1.5M. The ancillary equipment required to operate and control the system is approximately $0.5M of off the shelf components which includes controls racks, power meters, chillers and various personal and machine protection system hardware. Unfortunately, a key cost driver and technical development required for this test stand is the development of reliable key high power RF components such as windows, isolators, directional couplers and loads. Many of these items are not commercially available or have not been productized. Although RadiaBeam in collaboration with SLAC through the GRIT program, has manufactured many high power directional couplers and loads for their internal needs, these items are not available on the open market. Some development has also been undertaken for 50MW RF windows and is still in progress at the time of the writing, but have not been matured and fully high power tested. Finally isolators to handle 50MW power levels are still in development, with 20MW version from Microwave Techniques currently representing the state of the art for modest 2KW average power capacities. If the development of these C-band components can progress and be commercially available when such a high power test stand is required, the costs can be modest and in the range of $0.3M per station, however in the current state, it is expected to require approximately $1M of further developmental investment. Further, a very specialized and robust control system built on a PLC backbone and capable of safe automated conditioning is expected to require approximately $1.5M of developmental effort. Finally, another large expense will involve the construction of testing bunkers to manage the significant high energy radiation emitting from the structures during conditioning.
